key_insight: RL-generated rollouts may preserve knowledge usually thought to reside only in trained model weights. The paper explores recovering RL capabilities from these archived outputs, though the provided abstract is truncated before the findings.
problem_solved: RL pipelines typically discard rollouts after each update. This work asks whether those archives can instead become reusable training resources—and why simply replaying the original RL algorithm may fail.
method: Archive model-generated rollouts produced during RL post-training.
Investigate how much learned capability can be recovered by training on those archived rollouts.
Test replaying the original RL algorithm on archived rather than fresh rollouts; the excerpt indicates a failure but omits its details and the proposed remedy.
impact: Recovering capabilities from saved rollouts could make expensive RL-generated data reusable and reduce repeated generation costs. The supplied excerpt does not establish the achieved recovery rate or compute savings.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: RL training produces both updated model weights and an archive of rollouts.
Side-by-side workflows: fresh rollout generation versus archived rollout reuse.
Question-mark arrow from archived rollouts to a recovered model, highlighting the central research question.
Warning icon beside naive replay, indicating that straightforward reuse encounters a failure.
paper_title: Reinforcement Learning Can Be Recovered From Its Own Rollouts
paper_authors: Jiayi Sheng, Jingwen Gu, Guanning Zeng, Zhaoyi Zhou, Stefano Viel
